key_insight: A porous liquid droplet’s electrophoretic mobility is controlled by a single Brinkman-screened hydrodynamic resistance, creating a smooth bridge between clean-droplet and rigid-particle behavior.
engineering_relevance: This provides a tunable design rule for microfluidic and biomedical transport of soft charged droplets, where permeability, surface charge, and double-layer thickness can be adjusted to control motion.
method: Coupled Poisson-Nernst-Planck-Stokes equations outside the droplet with Brinkman-Debye-Bueche hydrodynamics inside.
Used a regular perturbation expansion in electric-field strength to reduce the problem to radial ODEs.
Derived a closed-form Debye-Hückel mobility expression and validated behavior beyond low potential with numerical solutions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical derivations plus numerical solutions over arbitrary Debye-layer thickness and beyond the low-potential regime, showing mobility can either increase or decrease with Darcy number.
watch_item: Permeability effects are non-universal: mobility trends can reverse depending on interfacial-velocity mode, dielectric polarization, and double-layer conditions, so design predictions require case-specific evaluation.
paper_title: Electrophoretic motion of a liquid droplet with Brinkman-screened internal hydrodynamics
